text:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: ONE seamless limestone base-color texture for a game material. A single full-frame square texture, requested 1536 x 1536 or higher native pixels, never an atlas, grid, contact sheet or multi-panel image. Opaque RGB image.

Only the surface of ONE continuous stone, covering a 1 meter by 1 meter patch. Pale light gray limestone with a very slight warm beige undertone, fine mineral grain, gentle wear and tiny scattered pores and shallow chips. Subtle softly mottled natural pigmentation, understated varied stone tones. The stone looks like authentic dry worn limestone paving material, with natural photo-real surface detail, neither plastic nor painterly. Fine detail rather than large pores, crack networks, marble veins or large holes.

This is an intrinsic ALBEDO/base-color material pass, not a lit photograph. Strict straight-down orthographic projection, no perspective. Absolutely even color response: no light direction, no cast shadows, no highlighted edges, no ambient-occlusion shading, no global gradient, no vignette or central glow. The shape of a slab is NOT shown. NO joints, grout, masonry, individual tiles, tile borders, slab edges, frames or divisions anywhere, even at the image edge. No dirt piles, moss, weeds, water, reflections, debris, footprints, writing, logos or marks.

Texture must be genuinely SEAMLESS and periodic in BOTH directions. Opposite sides match in color and microtexture, with features crossing the border continuing naturally on the opposite side. Design for a half-width plus half-height wrapped offset test: the centered horizontal and vertical wrap boundaries must have no visible line, change of texture density, abrupt color step or artificial symmetry. Use evenly distributed restrained fine-grained stochastic mineral detail and shallow surface variation, not a recognizable repeated motif. No outer border and no bright or dark edges. It must remain a convincing continuous single stone surface in a 4 by 4 repeat.

Output only this one flat light gray-beige stone color texture, filling the square edge to edge. Do not include normal, roughness, lighting preview, chart or text in this image.

Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: ONE full-frame tangent-space NORMAL MAP for the supplied limestone surface. The supplied image is a material reference and exact UV layout guide, not an edit target to patch locally. Generate a complete normal-data image of this same continuous stone surface. One square image only, native at least 1024 x 1024, preferably matching the reference 1254 x 1254. No atlas, inset, labels, margins or other maps. Opaque RGB.

Preserve the reference's exact framing, scale, UV positions and layout of tiny pores and shallow chips, so this normal map aligns with the supplied albedo. The surface covers one meter square. Fine limestone micrograin, gently worn subtle surface relief, tiny shallow concave pores. Pigmentation mottling is NOT large-scale geometry: keep the overall surface flat with no waves, broad raised lumps, cracks or ridges. No slab edges, no joints, no grout, no grid.

Output only OpenGL tangent normals, positive Y. Flat surface near RGB(128,128,255); blue/purple/cyan normal data, not a lit colored or gray photograph. Encode shallow stone relief, not ambient occlusion or color. Every vector points outward with positive Z; blue channel stays above 128, generally close to 255. Unit-length normal directions, with the R and G slopes balanced around 128, no global lighting bias. For a concave pore: left-side inward slope has R above 128, right side R below 128; top side G below 128, bottom side G above 128. This states OpenGL positive-Y with image rows going downward. Subtle physically plausible strength, not exaggerated spikes.

The normal field must remain seamlessly repeatable in X and Y and match the albedo's periodic layout. A 50% horizontal plus 50% vertical wrap-offset must show no central line, change in normal bias or texture density. Opposite edges must continue naturally. No directional illumination, shadows, highlights, vignette, borders, symbols, lettering or watermark. Fill the square with only the full-resolution normal map.

Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: ONE full-frame scalar ROUGHNESS MAP for the supplied dry limestone surface. Use the reference as the exact material and UV layout guide; generate the whole new data map, not a local patch. Single square image, native at least 1024 x 1024, preferably matching the reference 1254 x 1254. No atlas, inset, labels, margins or other maps. Opaque image with genuinely equal RGB grayscale channels.

Exactly match the reference framing, one-meter-square scale and positions of tiny pores and chips. The limestone is dry and matte, worn gently, with fine grain and restrained material variation. No stone boundaries, tile joints, slab edges, grout, grid, cracks, waves or 3D perspective.

This is LINEAR ROUGHNESS DATA, not a grayscale photograph, height map, ambient-occlusion map or smoothness map. Most stone should be medium-light gray around 0.72 roughness (about 184/255), with subtle natural variation roughly 0.65 to 0.80 and slightly rougher pore interiors around 0.85. No black recess shadows, bright specular spots, raised-rim shading or directional light. Color mottling should not be blindly copied into strong roughness contrast. Keep material variation restrained and aligned to the reference microstructure. Overall flat and evenly distributed material statistics.

Seamless periodic roughness in both directions: a wrapped 50%/50% offset reveals no central boundary, seam, sudden brightness change or change in grain density. No global gradient, vignette, dark edge, bright edge, symbols, text or watermark. Output only this complete scalar roughness texture filling the square.

reason: Correct the measured 24 negative-Z pixels and excess directional bias with complete low-amplitude normal regeneration.
text:
Create one complete new seamless tangent-space normal-data texture for the supplied continuous limestone surface. Exact same UV framing, pore locations, 1 x 1 meter coverage, square native 1254 x 1254 or at least 1024 x 1024. Output only the full-frame NORMAL MAP, no text, atlas, borders, presentation or other image.

This must be an EXTREMELY SUBTLE shallow-relief OpenGL POSITIVE Y normal field. Mostly neutral pale periwinkle RGB(128,128,255). All normals face the viewer with strong positive Z. BLUE CHANNEL MUST ALWAYS STAY ABOVE 220, INCLUDING THE CENTERS OF PORES. NO BLACK OR DARK BLUE DOTS. R and G stay near 128, most values between 110 and 146, and even at tiny pores between 90 and 166. Balance R and G symmetrically around 128 with no directional bias. Never paint an ambient occlusion shadow or literal dark hole into this normal map. Smooth flat interiors of the shallow pores also have the neutral normal RGB(128,128,255). ONLY the minute rim slopes carry a slight cyan or pink change. Do not invent broad waves, grooves or swollen geometry. The reference is pigment and fine limestone, with only extremely shallow relief.

For concave pore slopes under OpenGL positive Y: left inner rim R above 128; right inner rim R below 128; top inner rim G below 128; bottom inner rim G above 128. Keep changes very weak. No baked lighting or shadows anywhere. No grout, joints, tiles or slab edges. Seamless periodic X and Y, no visible center lines after 50 percent wrapped offset in both directions. Match edge texture statistics and continue pores across periodic boundaries. Whole new image using the supplied color map only as a matching surface guide. Native size, never an enlarged tiny atlas panel.

reason: Replace the shaded grayscale-photo-like candidate with a complete true low-contrast roughness-data generation.
text:
Generate ONE complete new scalar ROUGHNESS DATA MAP for the supplied dry matte limestone, exact same full-frame UV framing and 1 x 1 meter surface coverage. Native square 1254 x 1254 or at least 1024 x 1024. Full square only, no atlas, labels, border, text or other maps.

This is almost uniform medium-light gray material data, NOT a grayscale photograph. Flat quiet medium-light gray baseline RGB(190,190,190), with only faint low-contrast grain variation about 180 to 200. The microscopic pores are slightly MORE ROUGH, so their interiors should be slightly LIGHTER gray (about 205), NEVER black or dark. No dark holes, recessed shadows, lit rims, photographic shading, highlights, crack shadows or pigment copied from the reference. The image must NOT resemble a shaded monochrome photo of stone. Ignore the albedo color variations except as a guide to exact positions of tiny material pores. The reference does not provide illumination to copy. Use truly neutral grayscale, R=G=B at every pixel. Very restrained contrast; no values below 165 or above 215. Dry stone material is matte across the entire square.

No slabs, no edges, no grout, no joints or grid. Completely flat straight-on material data, no light direction and no vignette. Seamless periodic in both X and Y: a 50 percent wrap offset on both axes must reveal no central line or brightness discontinuity. The result should appear nearly uniform gray at a distance, with only faint scalar material variation up close. Create the whole new image.
